method: grouped by (user_login, performed_via_github_app slug or null) over issues.json and comments.json from evidence/repository-snapshots/<repo>/; login values ending in '[bot]' are flagged is_bot_account regardless of performed_via_github_app.
authorship_signal_caveat:
These counts are an exact tally of a raw API field combination, but as a signal about who authored an item they are asymmetric, not a complete census, AND the word 'direct' is ambiguous between two readings that this data answers differently — state which one is meant before quoting a bound:
(1) 'direct' = posted without a GitHub App intermediary. Under this reading, performed_via_github_app: null is an EXACT count of that property, and — since any PAT-holding process (gh CLI, an orchestrator, a harness) also yields null — it is an UPPER BOUND on human-typed comments (some or all of the null count may be process-posted).
(2) 'direct' = the human composed the text. Under this reading, null bounds nothing in either direction: a connector-attributed comment can carry text the human wrote verbatim, and a null comment can carry text an agent generated. Verifiable primary evidence for the latter: `gh api repos/uda-lab/KSE2026/issues/59/comments` shows comment ids 5071442579 ("Final proposal gate for head \u2026") and 5065764557 / 5066112755 / 5071134565 / 5071234655 / 5071326489 / 5071415951 ("@codex please review this PR") all posted under login `t-uda` with performed_via_github_app null and matching a repeated, formulaic workflow-notice pattern (consistent with automated posting, though this data alone cannot prove who or what posted them).
Conversely, a non-null performed_via_github_app slug IS a LOWER BOUND on mediated (connector-transmitted) authorship under reading (1), but proves only the transport channel under reading (2) — not who composed the prose, nor whether the human read it before it was posted. No client, user-agent, IP, session id, model version, or prompt is recoverable from this data. Comment edit history is not retroactively available, and deleted/minimized comments are absent from the export. Do not infer productivity, effectiveness, or causation from these counts.
